steps: Percentage of an amount: 10% is divide by 10, 1% is divide by 100; build the rest from these.
Increase or decrease with a multiplier: 20% up is × 1.2, 20% down is × 0.8.
Reverse percentage: divide the new amount by the multiplier to find the original.
method_card.title: Working with Percentages
method_card.content:
A percentage means 'out of 100', so 25% is \(\frac{25}{100} = 0.25\).

To grow or shrink an amount, use a multiplier: a 15% increase is × 1.15, a 15% decrease is × 0.85.

Reverse percentages give you the amount after a change and ask for the original: find the multiplier, then divide. After a 20% rise a price of £90 means original = 90 ÷ 1.2 = £75.
method_card.example:
A coat costs £60 after a 25% discount. Find the original price.

25% off means × 0.75, so original = \(60 \div 0.75 = 80\), that is £80.

steps: Reverse percentage: the amount you are given is a percentage of the original, not 100%. A price after a 5% rise is 105% of the original, so divide by 1.05.
Repeated changes: multiply the multipliers together. Up 20% then down 20% is × 1.2 × 0.8 = × 0.96, which is not back where you started.
Always check by working forwards from your answer.
gold.title: Gold: reverse and repeated change

example.question: After a 4% rise a rent is £624. Find the original rent.

steps: Find a percentage of a number. 10% is the number divided by 10, and 1% is divided by 100. Build the rest from these: 20% is two lots of 10%, and 5% is half of 10%.
Increase or decrease: find the percentage, then add it on or take it off.
Express as a percentage: divide the part by the whole, then multiply by 100.
bronze.title: Bronze: percentages of an amount

steps: Turn the change into a multiplier. A 15% increase gives 100% + 15% = 115%, so × 1.15. A 15% decrease gives 100% − 15% = 85%, so × 0.85.
Multiply the original by the multiplier in one step.
Reverse percentages: if you are given the amount after the change, divide by the multiplier to get back to the original.
silver.title: Silver: the multiplier method

gold.hint: £315 000 is 105% of the original, so divide by 1.05.
gold.display: A house increases in value by 5% to £315 000. Find the original value.

guided_steps.say: Reverse percentage on a big number. £315 000 is after a 5% rise, so it is 105% of the original.

guided_steps.hint: Add the rise to the original.

misconceptions.message: Do not subtract 5% of 315 000. Divide by 1.05: 315 000 ÷ 1.05 = 300 000.
Multiplier = 1.05. Original = 315 000 ÷ 1.05 = 300 000.

gold.hint: £14 450 is 85% of last year's value, so divide by 0.85.
gold.display: A car depreciates by 15% per year. It is now worth £14 450. What was it worth one year ago?

guided_steps.say: Reverse percentage. £14 450 is after a 15% fall, so it is 85% of last year's value.

guided_steps.done: One year ago it was worth £17 000.

misconceptions.message: Adding 15% of 14 450 gives the wrong amount. Divide by 0.85: 14 450 ÷ 0.85 = 17 000.
Depreciation is a decrease. Multiplier = 0.85. Original = 14 450 ÷ 0.85 = 17 000.

gold.display: A shop increases prices by 20% then has a 20% sale. An item now costs £48. Find the original price.

guided_steps.say: Two changes in a row: first +20% (× 1.2), then 20% off (× 0.8). Combine them.

guided_steps.done: £50 up then down lands on £48, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: Up 20% then down 20% does NOT cancel out. Combined multiplier: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, so original = 48 ÷ 0.96 = 50.
You reversed the sale but forgot the original 20% rise. Undo both: 48 ÷ 0.96 = 50, not 48 ÷ 0.8 = 60.

gold.hint: £21 000 is 87.5% of the original, so divide by 0.875.
gold.display: After a 12.5% pay cut, Priya earns £21 000. What was her original salary?

guided_steps.say: Reverse percentage with an awkward percentage. £21 000 is after a 12.5% cut, so it is 87.5% of the original.

misconceptions.message: Adding 12.5% of 21 000 is incorrect. Divide by 0.875: 21 000 ÷ 0.875 = 24 000.

gold.hint: £45.26 is 103% of the original, so divide by 1.03 and round to 2 d.p.
gold.display: A train fare goes up by 3% to £45.26. Find the original fare to the nearest penny.

guided_steps.say: Reverse percentage giving a decimal answer. £45.26 is after a 3% rise, so it is 103% of the original.

guided_steps.done: 43.94 grown by 3% rounds back to £45.26, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: Do not subtract 3% of 45.26. Divide: 45.26 ÷ 1.03 = 43.9417..., which rounds to £43.94.

bronze.hint: 25% is a quarter: halve the number, then halve again.

guided_steps.say: 25% means a quarter, which is half of a half. Set it up.

guided_steps.pre: Check by building up: 10% is 8, so 20% is 16 and 5% is 4; 16 + 4 =

misconceptions.message: You converted to a decimal but forgot to multiply. 0.25 × 80 = 20.
You divided by 0.25 instead of multiplying. 25% of 80 = 0.25 × 80 = 20.

guided_steps.say: 10% means 10 out of every 100, which is one tenth.

misconceptions.message: To find 10%, divide by 10. 350 ÷ 10 = 35.
That is 1% (divide by 100). For 10%, divide by 10: 350 ÷ 10 = 35.

guided_steps.say: 50% means half. Split 126 into 100 + 26 to halve it in your head.

guided_steps.done: Doubling gets back to 126, so 50% of 126 = 63.

misconceptions.message: 50% means half, so divide by 2, not multiply by 2. 126 ÷ 2 = 63.

bronze.hint: 15% is 10% plus 5%: find 10%, halve it, and add.

guided_steps.say: 15% is 10% plus 5%. Build it up.

bronze.hint: Divide the part by the whole, then multiply by 100.
bronze.display: Express 18 out of 60 as a percentage

guided_steps.say: Turn '18 out of 60' into a fraction of 1, then scale to 100.

guided_steps.pre: Multiply by 100 to get a percentage: 0.3 × 100 =

guided_steps.done: 30% of 60 is 18, so the answer fits.

misconceptions.message: Divide part by whole: 18 ÷ 60 = 0.3. Then × 100 = 30%.

bronze.hint: Find 10% of 80, then take it off.

guided_steps.say: Decrease means find the percentage, then take it off.

misconceptions.message: That is a 10% increase. For a decrease: 80 × 0.9 = 72.
Do not subtract 10 from 80. Find 10% of 80 (= 8), then subtract: 80 − 8 = 72.

bronze.hint: Find 20% of 150, then add it on.

guided_steps.say: Increase means find the percentage, then add it on.

misconceptions.message: 30 is the increase amount, but the question asks for the total. 150 + 30 = 180.
That is a 20% decrease. For an increase: 150 × 1.2 = 180.

bronze.hint: 5% is half of 10%: find 10%, then halve it.

guided_steps.say: 5% is half of 10%. Find 10% first.

misconceptions.message: That is 10%. For 5%, halve it: 64 ÷ 2 = 32.

silver.hint: Multiply by 1.15, or find 15% and add it on.

guided_steps.say: The multiplier method: a 15% increase leaves you with 115% of the money.

misconceptions.message: Do not add 15 directly. 15% of 350 = 52.50, so the total is 350 + 52.50 = 402.50.

silver.hint: A 35% decrease leaves 65%, so multiply by 0.65.

guided_steps.say: A 35% decrease leaves 65% behind. Build that multiplier.

misconceptions.message: That is a 35% increase. For a decrease: 480 × 0.65 = 312.
Decrease multiplier: 1 − 0.35 = 0.65. Then 480 × 0.65 = 312.

guided_steps.say: Make a fraction, then scale it to 100.

guided_steps.done: A quarter of 180 is 45, so 25% is right.

silver.hint: £315 is 90% of the original, so divide by 0.9.
silver.display: A phone costs £315 after a 10% discount. Find the original price.

guided_steps.say: Reverse percentage. £315 is the price after 10% off, so it is 90% of the original.

guided_steps.done: £350 with 10% off is £315, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: Adding 10% of 315 gives the wrong answer. The original is higher: divide by the multiplier, 315 ÷ 0.9 = 350.
10% discount gives multiplier 0.9. Original = 315 ÷ 0.9 = 350.

silver.hint: Divide the change by the original, then multiply by 100.
silver.display: A population grows from 250 to 310. What is the percentage increase?

guided_steps.say: Percentage change compares the change with the original.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract the old value from the new.

misconceptions.message: Divide the change by the ORIGINAL (250), not the new value (310). 60 ÷ 250 × 100 = 24%.
Do not forget to multiply by 100. 0.24 × 100 = 24%.

silver.hint: £480 is 120% of the pre-VAT price, so divide by 1.2.
silver.display: VAT is 20%. A laptop costs £480 including VAT. Find the price before VAT.

guided_steps.say: Reverse percentage. £480 includes 20% VAT, so it is 120% of the pre-VAT price.

guided_steps.done: £400 plus 20% VAT is £480, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: Subtracting 20% of 480 is wrong: 480 already includes VAT. Divide by 1.2: 480 ÷ 1.2 = 400.
20% added gives multiplier 1.2. Original = 480 ÷ 1.2 = 400.

silver.hint: £28 is 70% of the original, so divide by 0.7.
silver.display: A shirt is reduced by 30%. It now costs £28. Find the original price.

guided_steps.say: Reverse percentage. £28 is the price after 30% off, so it is 70% of the original.

guided_steps.done: £40 with 30% off is £28, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: Adding 30% of 28 is wrong. 28 is 70% of the original. Divide by 0.7: 28 ÷ 0.7 = 40.
30% decrease gives multiplier 0.7. Original = 28 ÷ 0.7 = 40.
